title: BUILD 1 -- MAKE THE HEAD FREE.  Capturing the generator-frame hidden states during generation instead of recomputing them with a teacher-forced pass
objective: The new round objective is 'a small trained verifier improves a 7B medical VLM by +X on N cells at Y x the 7B's own compute'.  The generator-frame head costs 3.813646 forward passes per question (= 8943 distinct normalised answers / 2345 questions) purely to recompute hidden states the generator already produced. This build tests whether capturing them during generation reproduces the head's scores and picks, and what that removes from Y.

harness_reproduces_the_frozen_feature_ca.note: this is the MATCHED IN-SESSION CONTROL the project's +-0.008 regeneration caveat requires: every captured arm is compared against a teacher-forced arm computed in the same session, same box, same numerics.

DELIVERABLE_1_capture.how: src/training_methods/free_head_capture.py drives model.generate() from the PROMPT ONLY with a LogitsProcessor forcing the stored candidate's token ids, then reads layer-21 hidden states out of generate()'s own per-step outputs.  That is the real generation code path -- prefill, then one cached decode step per token -- so the captured states are what a deployed capture would see, while the token sequence is guaranteed to be the stored candidate rather than a fresh sample.
DELIVERABLE_1_capture.definition_identical_to_the_trained_head: same base Lingshu-7B (no adapter), same SYS_GEN answering prompt, same layer 21, same span = mean over the candidate's own tokens, same fp16 storage, same row keys. extract_generator_hidden.build_eval_rows / .encode are IMPORTED, not re-implemented.

cap320.note_boundary: boundary_ok: tokenising prompt+answer gives prompt_ids + tokenise(answer) exactly, so the span the head reads is exactly the candidate's tokens and the AR path can force the identical ids.

fullres.note_boundary: boundary_ok: tokenising prompt+answer gives prompt_ids + tokenise(answer) exactly, so the span the head reads is exactly the candidate's tokens and the AR path can force the identical ids.

1_the_head_is_free_and_the_picks_barely_.claim: capturing layer-21 h_span out of model.generate()'s own per-step hidden states reproduces the frozen head's endpoint. At the resolution the head was trained on (fullres) the capture changes 15 of 2345 picks; at the resolution the DEPLOYED pools were generated at (cap320) it changes 153 of 2345, and neither is a significant move in EITHER currency.
1_the_head_is_free_and_the_picks_barely_.why: the definition, the span and the causal mask are identical; the residual is bf16 kernel arithmetic, because a prefill over many positions and a KV-cached decode of one position reduce in different orders. The proof that this is the only cause is the harness null test: the SAME script's teacher-forced pass reproduced the frozen cache bit-identically on 8943 of 8943 rows, so the pipeline itself is deterministic.

2_cost.what_is_left: with the head free the open arm's remaining cost is N generations plus the LoRA verifier's own passes. The verifier is the ONLY thing that still has to be paid for, and it cannot be captured from the generator the way the head can, because its adapter changes the weights.

3_head_only_is_NOT_a_safe_replacement_fo.claim: the round brief's premise -- the head alone (0.7956) beats the LoRA verifier (0.7752), so dropping the LoRA is cheaper AND better -- is REFUTED by the second currency. The head-alone advantage is judge-only and REVERSES under exact match.
3_head_only_is_NOT_a_safe_replacement_fo.also_note: 0.7956 is a SINGLE-SEED fit; the frozen 8-seed ensemble head alone is 0.801090 (judge). See per_seed_head_only.

4_vs_the_new_always_7b_baseline.arm: fusion on captured cap320 features (the free head, at the deployed generation geometry), best-of-8
4_vs_the_new_always_7b_baseline.cells: 3 of the 8 macro cells. The other 5 are multiple-choice-as-presented and carry no open-text candidate pool; they are neither claimed nor charged.

HOLES: The capture was driven through HF transformers' model.generate(). The DEPLOYED pools were generated with vLLM, which does not expose per-step hidden states through its standard API. 'The head is free' is proven for the HF generation path and is an ENGINEERING task, not a scientific one, for the vLLM path. NOT MEASURED: a vLLM capture.

The candidates were FORCED to the stored token ids with a LogitsProcessor so the comparison is exactly paired. A live deployment captures the states of whatever it actually samples; those are the same states by construction, but this run does not re-sample, so no fresh generation and no +-0.008 exposure is incurred.

The head was TRAINED on fullres features while the deployed pools are GENERATED at cap320, so a free capture necessarily feeds the head out-of-distribution features. Measured cost of that mismatch at the fusion level: -0.0008528784648187404 (judge) / 0.0017057569296374808 (em), both TIE. At the HEAD-ONLY level it is larger and the judge arm becomes a LOSS vs deployed fusion. NOT MEASURED: refitting the head on cap320 features, which is the obvious repair.

N=8 fixed. The deployed arm draws adaptive N (meanN 4.371-6.630); the head's pass count at smaller N is given as a MEASURED curve in cost.distinct_answers_vs_sample_budget, but the Weitzman policy's per-question N is not reproduced here, so no single adaptive-N FLOP-eq number is claimed.

This build changes the COST of the selector, not its accuracy. It does not by itself bring the open arm's Y near 1: best-of-8 fusion is still 11.823 FLOP-eq as-charged with the head free. The remaining levers are N (T=0.4 at N=4 already beats T=0.7 at N=8) and the LoRA verifier's N-times-repeated image prefill.
